status_summary: A presidential memorandum of 2025-09-09 directed the HHS Secretary to improve transparency and accuracy in direct-to-consumer drug advertising, including more risk information, and the FDA Commissioner to enforce the advertising provisions of the drug law. The same day HHS and FDA announced thousands of letters to drug makers, about 100 planned cease-and-desist letters, review of sponsored social media posts and rulemaking to end the adequate provision option for broadcast ads. The Unified Agenda lists FDA's Transparency in Direct-to-Consumer Advertising rule (RIN 0910-AJ14) at the proposed rule stage with a proposal expected in December 2026, as an economically significant, major rule. No proposed rule had been published as of 2026-10-13.

uncertainties: GovInfo notes that an original copy of the memorandum was not available for verification. Counts of letters come from a law-firm summary of the HHS and FDA announcement; the FDA press release was not opened, and a later law-firm report gives about 100 cease-and-desist and about 40 untitled letters.
